---
title: "Week 4: Social Cohesion and Health"
---

## Theme: Collective Efficacy, Trust, and Community Health

Robert Sampson\'s landmark Chicago research established that collective
efficacy --- a neighborhood\'s shared willingness to intervene for the
common good --- is one of the strongest predictors of health and safety
outcomes, independent of poverty. This week we map social vulnerability
alongside CDC PLACES health outcome data, focusing on variables that
capture social isolation and lack of emotional support --- dimensions of
health that are often invisible in administrative data. We build
bivariate maps that visually communicate the relationship between
neighborhood social conditions and population health.

## Classroom Lab Demonstration

**Legal Focus:** Home Rule and local governance authority; Fair Housing
Act and exclusionary zoning; legal frameworks for community health
investment; ARPA (American Rescue Plan Act) and community health block
grant allocation criteria.

**Health Focus:** CDC PLACES health outcome data, specifically the
\'Lack of Social and Emotional Support\' measure (CASTHMA model) and
\'Mental Health Not Good\' variable --- two outcomes that track closely
with neighborhood collective efficacy and social isolation.

**Data:** CDC Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), 2020, available at
atsdr.cdc.gov/placeandhealth/svi; CDC PLACES Local Data for Better
Health (tract-level), available at cdc.gov/places --- specifically
variables CASTHMA (current asthma), MHLTH (mental health), SOCIAL (lack
of social and emotional support), and CSMOKING.

**R Code:** Read SVI and PLACES CSV files; merge by GEOID using
dplyr::left_join(); biscale package for bivariate choropleth
(biscale::bi_class(), bi_legend()); ggplot2 geom_sf() with two-variable
color encoding; cowplot::plot_grid() to combine map and legend.

- Load CDC SVI 2020 data and CDC PLACES tract-level data for Ohio, both
  available as CSV download from CDC websites

- Merge SVI and PLACES by census tract GEOID using dplyr::left_join()

- Produce Bivariate Map 1: SVI overall score (x-axis) vs. PLACES \'Lack
  of Social and Emotional Support\' (SOCIAL variable, y-axis) using
  biscale package; identify tracts in the High-High quadrant

- Produce Bivariate Map 2: SVI overall score (x-axis) vs. PLACES
  \'Mental Health Not Good\' (MHLTH variable, y-axis); compare
  geographic pattern to Map 1

- Discuss: which tracts appear as high-burden on both maps? What does
  the spatial pattern suggest about where collective efficacy is lowest?
